description: A single-panel X-ray diffraction figure consisting of five stacked patterns of Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni low-density steel SLM-printed at different laser powers. The y-axis is Intensity (a.u.) with no numeric scale printed; the x-axis is 2θ (degree) spanning 30° to 100° with major ticks every 10°. From bottom to top the traces are colour-coded P-70 (red), P-90 (gold), P-110 (green), P-130 (light blue) and P-150 (dark blue). Five reflections are annotated above the topmost pattern with black filled dots — (111) just above the 40° gridline, (200) at the 50° gridline, (220) roughly a third of the way between 70° and 80°, (311) just below 90°, and (222) between 90° and 100° — and the top-right legend key identifies the black-dot symbol as γ-Fe(M). All five patterns contain only these γ-Fe(M) fcc reflections; no α-Fe(M) peak is labelled or apparent anywhere, so the figure demonstrates that the printed alloy is essentially fully austenitic at every laser power. The (111) reflection is the strongest throughout, and the peaks appear progressively sharper/narrower from the bottom red P-70 trace to the top dark-blue P-150 trace. No numeric intensities, d-spacings or peak positions are printed on the figure.
measured_quantities: Intensity (a.u.) — relative only, no numeric scale
FWHM of the (111) γ-Fe(M) peak (values quoted in text; unit not stated)

observations.observation: The figure is one XRD panel in which five diffractograms are stacked vertically: P-70 (red, bottom), P-90 (gold), P-110 (green), P-130 (light blue) and P-150 (dark blue, top).
Axes are Intensity (a.u.) on the y-axis (no numeric scale printed) against 2θ (degree) from 30° to 100° with major ticks every 10°.
Five reflections are annotated with black filled dots: (111) just above the 40° tick, (200) at the 50° tick, (220) between the 70° and 80° ticks, (311) just below 90°, and (222) between 90° and 100°.
The legend key at top right labels the black filled dot as γ-Fe(M), i.e. the marked reflections are assigned to the austenite (fcc) phase.
No reflection labelled or attributable to α-Fe(M) appears in any of the five patterns; only the five γ-Fe(M) peaks are marked.
The (111) reflection near the 40° tick is the strongest peak in all five patterns; the (200) peak near 50° is the second strongest and the (220), (311) and (222) peaks are progressively weaker.
The (111) diffraction peak appears progressively narrower/sharper from the bottom P-70 trace to the top P-150 trace, although no FWHM values are printed on the figure.
The figure contains no numeric y-axis intensities, peak positions or d-spacings; all quantitative peak data are absent from the pixels.
The caption states that the patterns are of Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni samples SLM-printed at various laser powers.
The text states that, in contrast to the Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni powder, the SLM-printed alloy at each laser power mainly comprises the austenite phase without any α-Fe(M) phase.
The text reports FWHM values of the (111) peak of 0.289, 0.274, 0.263, 0.255 and 0.237 for P-70, P-90, P-110, P-130 and P-150 respectively (no unit given in the citing sentence).
The text interprets the decreasing (111) FWHM with increasing laser power as an increase in average grain size caused by a slower cooling rate and longer grain-growth period at higher energy density.

The figure's evidentiary role is to show that all five laser-power conditions produce a single-phase austenitic (γ-Fe(M)) structure, while the peak-broadening trend it displays supports the grain-growth argument made in the text.

subfigures.description: Stacked XRD patterns (Intensity (a.u.) vs 2θ = 30–100°) of five Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni SLM samples labelled P-70, P-90, P-110, P-130, P-150 from bottom to top; reflections (111), (200), (220), (311), (222) are annotated with black dots keyed in the legend as γ-Fe(M). No α-Fe(M) peaks are present. The (111) peak narrows visibly from P-70 towards P-150.
